# AttackMap

> AttackMap is local-first, AI-assisted defensive security analysis for codebases. It maps a repository's attack surface, traces request-to-sink data flow, scores exploitability, and writes a prioritized, evidence-grounded review. Output is aimed entirely at remediation. Status: beta; under active development, but progress may be slow until more contributors join.

AttackMap installs from GitHub (`pipx install git+https://github.com/mlaify/AttackMap.git`) and needs Python 3.11 or later. Source: https://github.com/mlaify/AttackMap (MIT). Security reports: security@mlaify.io.

- [Home](https://docs.mlaify.io/): What AttackMap does and where to go next.

- [Quickstart](https://docs.mlaify.io/quickstart/): A first scan and how to read the reports.

- [Scanning & output](https://docs.mlaify.io/scanning/): The analyze command, output artifacts, anomaly and invariant mining, recall mode, fleet analysis, and baseline diff gating.

- [CI & pull requests](https://docs.mlaify.io/ci/): The GitHub Action, PR bot, SARIF, and gating.
- [macOS app](https://docs.mlaify.io/gui/): The native front end that drives the CLI.
